title: ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Fans, Rejoice! Dónal Finn Will Be Back for Three-Part Christmas Special
summary: Mary Bennet's beloved husband, Tom Hayward, is officially back for the much-anticipated special. But so is his rival!

title: How to Run a Microcinema with John Wilson
summary: Filmmaker John Wilson tells IndieWire about helping to run the Low Cinema in Queens while also working on his new film “The History of Concrete."

title: ‘The Daughters of Abraham’ Review: Individualism and Community Test Each Other’s Limits in an Interfaith Friendship Drama
summary: TIFF: Hanaël El Yousfi's feature debut follows the ongoing relationship between a Jewish woman and her Muslim friend, illustrating how the conflicting desires for independence and family connection are universal.

title: Trying to Picture Doomsday? 1983’s ‘WarGames’ Already Showed Us One Way AI Could End the World
summary: After a former Anthropic researcher warned that humanity's extinction could be as close as 2030, John Badham’s cyber thriller offers a frighteningly clear answer to the question: "OK, how?"

title: Phil Lord and Chris Miller to Deliver Keynote Conversation at IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking Summit
summary: The "Project Hail Mary" directors and producers will explain how they made their most challenging blockbuster yet at the Los Angeles summit on October 17.

title: ‘Best of the Best’ Pulls Off the Perfect Heist Through Its Dance Numbers
summary: Director Lena Khan; choreographers Phillip Chbeeb, Makenzie Dustman, and Joya Kazi; and DP Adam Carboni tell IndieWire about dances that contain every facet of the characters — just like a diamond stolen by the British.

title: Mike Leigh Movies Always Start Without a Script. Watch the ‘Tender Loving Care’ Director and Cast Break Down His Unique Filmmaking Process
summary: At a TIFF dinner co-hosted by IndieWire and Bleecker Street, Leigh and his longtime collaborators opened up about a lifetime spent creating characters together.

title: ‘NAZA,’ Israeli Military Doc from ‘No Other Land’ Directors, Sets Speedy Fall Release in U.S.
summary: The controversial documentary is moving ahead with a self-distribution strategy that will roll the film out across American cities beginning in October.

title: ‘Monster,’ the TV Show, Devolves Into a Poor Impersonation of ‘Monster’ the Movie
summary: Season 4 of Ryan Murphy's gruesome Netflix anthology is ostensibly about Lizzie Borden, but its side story involving Aileen Wuornos — memorably realized by Charlize Theron in the 2003 film — shows how little the series has to say about either killer.

title: Aaron Sorkin Was His Own ‘Second Choice’ to Direct ‘The Social Reckoning’ — David Fincher Was His First
summary: Sorkin tells IndieWire about changing his mind on "not wanting to jump up and down" on Zuckerberg again and why this is not a "Social Network" sequel.

title: You’ve Never Seen Saoirse Ronan Quite Like This Before
summary: In Jonatan Etzler's darkly funny "Bad Apples," the actress plays a harried teacher who does something really crazy to a naughty student. As the pair explain to IndieWire, that's not the wildest part: It's how disarmingly funny Ronan gets to be.

title: ‘Youth’ Review: Sharon Horgan’s Sharp HBO Comedy Asks What We Really Have to Sacrifice with Age
summary: The "Catastrophe" writer and star returns to HBO (post-"Divorce") with a mid-life crisis comedy that's broadly familiar but refreshing in its specific insights, strong performances, and steady laughs.
